facts.label: Leverage trajectory and drivers
facts.text: Total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.73x at year-end 2025 to 2.26x at 2026-09-30, but net debt to adjusted EBITDA moved from 1.70x to 1.73x, so the gross improvement did not reach net leverage. The cause is mechanical: the issuer redeemed the USD 379.15 million 7.50% notes and USD 100.00 million of the 9.125% notes from cash, cutting principal by USD 479.15 million, while cash fell by USD 465.64 million and net debt moved only from USD 1,553.97 million to USD 1,547.69 million. Last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA was USD 912.67 million at year-end and USD 893.57 million at 2026-09-30, so earnings did not drive the change; for creditors the gain is a lower interest bill and no maturity in 2026 to 2028, not a stronger net position. facts.label: Reported and adjusted EBITDA
facts.text: The two EBITDA measures point in opposite directions because FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 1,402.13 million contains a USD 413.96 million gain on the Quail Tools sale and a USD 113.65 million bargain purchase gain on the Parker acquisition. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore looks like 1.78x at year-end and rises to 2.22x by 2026-09-30, while the adjusted ratio falls from 2.73x to 2.26x; by 2026-09-30 the gains have left the twelve-month window and the two ratios sit close together. Adjusted EBITDA is the better trend measure but not a cash one: it excludes Other, net, a cost of USD 65.80 million in FY2025 that included debt buyback losses, severance and impairments, and the issuer itself says the measure excludes certain cash expenses it is obliged to make. facts.label: Coverage
facts.text: Cash interest cover can be stated only for FY2025: 4.36x on adjusted EBITDA and 6.70x on reported EBITDA against USD 209.17 million of cash paid for interest, net of capitalized interest. The interim reports print no cash interest, so for the three 2026 dates the nearest evidence is interest expense, which fell from USD 215.37 million in FY2025 to USD 179.15 million on a twelve-month basis at 2026-09-30 as notes were retired, lifting adjusted EBITDA to interest expense from 4.24x to 4.99x. The issuer reports a credit agreement interest coverage ratio that rose from 4.16x at year-end to 5.20x at 2026-09-30 against a 2.75x minimum, but headroom is not worked here because the covenant's EBITDA definition is not supplied. The four notes outstanding at 2026-09-30 carry coupons of USD 156.75 million a year, covered 5.70x by twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, so cash interest on the current notes should run well below the 2025 level, before revolver fees and other items (analyst judgement). facts.label: Debt structure and claims outside debt
facts.text: All USD 2,050.00 million of principal is fixed-rate notes: USD 250.00 million of 1.75% exchangeable notes due June 2029, USD 550.00 million of 9.125% notes due January 2030, USD 550.00 million of 8.875% notes due August 2031 and USD 700.00 million of 7.625% notes due November 2032. The undrawn revolver, secured by a first lien on land rigs and related equipment, spare parts and inventory in the contiguous United States, matures on 2029-06-17 or 90 days before the exchangeable notes mature if 50% or more of them remain outstanding, so the first dated demand on the structure is in 2029. The exchangeable notes had a fair value of USD 230.31 million, 92.13% of principal, at 2026-09-30. Claims outside the debt figure are the redeemable noncontrolling interest of USD 502.72 million (mezzanine equity, Saudi Aramco's share of the redeemable ownership interests in SANAD, with USD 20.27 million of distributions accrued in nine months), operating lease liabilities of USD 40.21 million at year-end, purchase commitments of USD 296.4 million, letters of credit of USD 133.447 million under bilateral facilities and USD 68.2 million under the credit agreement, financial standby letters of credit and surety instruments of USD 33.795 million at most, which may overlap the letters of credit, receivables sold of USD 168.0 million, and contract liabilities of USD 100.02 million, up from USD 70.57 million at year-end, a non-debt float that helps fund working capital. No pension or retiree medical obligation is separately stated in the balance sheet lines supplied; only pension amortisation appears in other comprehensive income. facts.label: Strongest contrary evidence
facts.text: The strongest case against reading leverage as improving is that net debt has not fallen: USD 1,547.69 million against USD 1,553.97 million at year-end, with adjusted EBITDA flat and cash USD 465.64 million lower. SANAD newbuild spending of USD 295 million to USD 305 million is guided for 2026, five SANAD rigs have been suspended, and 41% of receivables are in Saudi Arabia. A fourth quarter below the guided adjusted free cash flow of USD 60 million to USD 70 million, or further rig suspensions that cut adjusted EBITDA, would leave cash falling while net leverage rises; continued adjusted free cash flow near the third-quarter level of USD 74.52 million would support the improving reading. limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- High: Cash paid for interest is printed only in the annual report (USD 209.167 million for FY2025). The three 2026 quarterly reports print none, so cash interest cover is not calculable at 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 and the interest expense ratios are proxies. Interim cash paid for interest, or the issuer's own figure, would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-03-31_nbr-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_nbr-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5. - High: No source states the ranking or security of the 1.75% exchangeable notes, the 9.125% notes, the 8.875% notes or the 7.625% notes beyond the words in their titles, and the guarantors are not listed, so the debt stack shows only the revolver and the notes are left out of any secured or senior subtotal. The indentures named in the exhibit index would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 135–136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15. - Medium: The annual report describes the covenant as four-quarter EBITDA over four-quarter interest expense but does not define EBITDA, and the collateral coverage threshold is not printed, so the reported interest coverage ratio (5.20x at 2026-09-30) cannot be reconciled to the twelve-month adjusted EBITDA over interest expense of 4.99x and covenant headroom is not worked. The executed credit agreement would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 40. - Medium: Figures are consolidated and include SANAD, whose cash was USD 180.635 million of USD 475.072 million at 2026-09-30; no obligor-group or restricted-group financials are supplied, so a borrower-level view of cash and EBITDA is not established. Group-level financials would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2. - Medium: The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA and no FY2025 adjusted EBITDA: reported EBITDA is calculated from components and FY2025 adjusted EBITDA is calculated by the issuer's definition, equal to the stated nine months 2025 plus fourth quarter 2025. The 2025 gains of USD 527.615 million make the reported ratios at the first three dates unsuitable for trend; an issuer statement of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA would confirm it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_tm2612942d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–11; calculation C4. - Low: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split in any supplied document and cash taxes paid are printed for FY2025 only (USD 73.738 million), so cash flow after maintenance spending and cash tax cover are not established for the 2026 dates. Interim supplemental cash flow disclosures would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 43. - Low: Several statement lines print a dash or are not printed in some columns: the Quail Tools and bargain purchase gains in the 2026 income statements, the current portion of debt, contract liabilities at 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, and a number of cash flow lines (impairments, cash acquired in the Parker business combination, revolver borrowings and repayments, the Parker dividend, SPAC redemptions, the Quail Tools proceeds and the Vast investment). Each is shown as not supplied and none is read as zero; the issuer's own totals and reconciliations show them to be nil. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_nbr-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_nbr-20260630x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 82–84. - Low: The debt note prints no per-instrument carrying value (the fair value note prints principal under that heading) and no revolver reference rate, spread or floor; carrying value is stated in aggregate only, net of deferred financing costs, and the exact maturity days of three of the notes are not printed. The indentures and the credit agreement would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 103. - Low: Fourth quarter 2025 stands alone only as the comparative column of the first-quarter release and is unaudited; it is used in the chart and dashboard, not in any ratio. The fourth-quarter release is not supplied. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-04-28_tm2612942d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6. - Low: Noncurrent operating lease liabilities are printed for 2025-12-31 only (USD 30.473 million); the interim reports print the current portion alone, so the lease claim at 2026-09-30 is not established. The interim lease note would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2. - Low: The first and second quarterly reports date the credit agreement joinder April 4, 2026 in the liquidity discussion and April 7, 2026 elsewhere; April 7, 2026 is used and no amount is affected. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_nbr-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_nbr-20260331x10q.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16.

Most contracts are daywork contracts at a dayrate, term contracts last from six months to five years, single-well contracts can be ended on short notice, and early termination payments may not fully compensate; no backlog or rig-level contract schedule is supplied, so durability is judged from rig counts and margins only.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Capital allocation has favoured creditors in 2026, not clearly in 2025. In the first nine months of 2026 principal fell by USD 479.15 million, paid from cash on hand, while in 2025 the USD 902.68 million of debt repaid was largely refinanced with USD 700.0 million of new notes and revolver borrowings, leaving principal only USD 10.46 million lower. The issuer paid no common dividend in the cash flow statements for 2023 to 2025, bought Parker with shares and USD 0.6 million of cash, and sold Quail Tools for net consideration of USD 600.0 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 133. - High: The joint venture agreement and the contracts with Saudi Aramco are not supplied, so the call option, the backstop and the terms of the redeemable interests are known only from filing summaries and the partner's leverage over Nabors cannot be sized. The executed agreement would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 114. - High: The indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so restricted payment capacity, guarantor coverage and the ranking and security of the notes are not established beyond the filing summaries. The executed documents would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16. - Medium: Amounts and approval terms for the Hexegen profit sharing and the director-affiliated services are not stated beyond the USD 14.8 million of services in 2025, so related-party leakage cannot be sized. The proxy statement's related-person section would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 114. - Medium: No customer backlog, contract expiry schedule or rig-level dayrate is supplied, so revenue durability and concentration beyond Saudi Aramco cannot be tested. Customer contract schedules would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 21. - Medium: The dates and contract effect of the five SANAD rig suspensions are not stated, so the near-term earnings effect of the newbuild program cannot be dated. The next release or investor presentation would close it. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3. - Low: The use of the Quail Tools proceeds and the funding source of each redemption are not itemised, so the link between asset-sale cash and debt reduction is inferred from the cash flow statement. The cash flow notes would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 96. - Low: The consideration for the Quail Tools sale is stated as net consideration of USD 600.0 million, while cash of USD 375.0 million and a seller note of USD 250.0 million add to USD 625.0 million; the difference is not explained and the cash flow statement shows USD 622.856 million of proceeds. The sale agreement would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 83. - Low: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split, so free cash flow durability after the SANAD newbuild program is not established. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a stronger credit is the pace of operating improvement and the deferral of maturities: quarterly adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 221.56 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 to USD 245.54 million in the third quarter of 2026, management guides about USD 930.00 million for 2026 and an annualised run rate near USD 1 billion going into 2027, no principal falls due before 2029, and the interest coverage ratio reported to lenders rose from 4.16x to 5.20x. The strongest evidence for a weaker credit is that net leverage has not fallen, free cash flow is small after growth capital spending, and about half of revenue is international with one counterparty at its centre. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical, partly concentrated and pricing-sensitive: operators award most work by bid, competition is price-led with excess rig supply historically, and US operators have kept activity flat while gaining drilling efficiency, so rig counts need not rise with the oil price. Against that, leading-edge Lower 48 pricing is rising, average rigs working rose from the second quarter to the third quarter of 2026, and International Drilling's daily adjusted gross margin rose to USD 19,060, so margin per rig day, not rig count, is the near-term driver. Saudi Aramco's per-rig contracts at about 30% of FY2025 revenue make Saudi activity the single largest revenue sensitivity. facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense and sets pricing: the annual report names Helmerich & Payne, Patterson-UTI, Precision and Ensign as rivals and says contracts are mostly bid, so pricing power is limited to periods of tight supply. New entry is limited by the capital needed for modern rigs, but rigs move between regions, so excess capacity can be imported; substitution takes the form of efficiency and automation, which lower the number of rigs needed per unit of output. Buyers are large and informed, and Saudi Aramco is both buyer and joint venture owner, which gives it more leverage than a normal customer; supplier power is low for rig equipment because Nabors makes its own through Canrig. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The issuer-specific downside begins with a cut in Saudi Arabian activity: the Middle East conflict has already led operators to issue suspension notices and five SANAD rigs are suspended, so a wider cut would first lower rig days and daily margin in International Drilling, 53.05% of revenue. Because direct costs are 62.24% of revenue and depreciation does not flex, EBITDA would fall faster than revenue; free cash flow, already thin at USD 38.65 million over nine months, would turn negative unless capital spending falls, and receivables from Saudi Arabia, 41% of the balance, would rise as payment slows. Liquidity of USD 825.07 million would fall as cash funds the gap, and the receivables programme ending by 2027-04-01 could add up to USD 168.0 million of funding need; management can cut growth capital spending at SANAD, but the backstop of the first 25 rigs limits that lever. Leverage would rise toward the covenant tests, whose definitions are not supplied, but no maturity falls due before 2029, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months and the first observable triggers are further suspensions, Saudi collections and fourth-quarter free cash flow. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Nabors presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, technology breadth, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before 2029, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow, concentration in Saudi Aramco and the SANAD joint venture, and note priority that is not established. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 170.44 million over four quarters. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding adjusted EBITDA near USD 930.00 million, cutting growth capital spending after the newbuild program, and renewing the receivables programme. The primary downside path is a cut in Saudi activity reaching revenue, joint venture cash and covenants together. Further analysis would require the indentures, the credit agreement, the joint venture agreement and the proxy statement. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings are sufficient for the credit snapshot's financial foundation, business profile and fundamental credit view of Nabors as of November 5, 2026, but not for conclusions that depend on executed debt documents, agency ratings or dated prices for the notes.

The latest filing is the quarterly report for September 30, 2026, signed one day before the as-of date, and the filings cover four consecutive quarters back to the fourth quarter of 2025. Figures are consolidated for Nabors Industries Ltd. and include the Saudi land drilling joint venture SANAD, which holds 38.02% of consolidated cash and cash equivalents, so cash and debt are not a view of the borrowing group alone.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 46; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_tm2612942d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation C1; calculation C8.

Covenant levels and guarantor structure rest on the filings' own summaries, ratings are described only as non-investment grade, and ownership and governance detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

- Material: Executed debt documents are not supplied. Covenant definitions, guarantor lists, the collateral coverage threshold and the security of each note therefore rest on the filings' own summaries or are not printed, and Fundamental credit must label its statements on covenants, guarantees and priority as summaries until the executed documents are supplied.

- Material: No financial statements for the borrowing group alone are supplied. The statements are consolidated and include SANAD, whose cash and cash equivalents were 38.02% of the consolidated amount at September 30, 2026, and no obligor-group or restricted-group summary appears. - Minor: Agency ratings are not established. The documents say only that the senior unsecured debt is rated non-investment grade, with no agency, symbol, outlook or action date; current ratings would be needed for any ratings-based conclusion.

- Minor: Dated market prices for the notes, a peer set, a portfolio and fund limits are not supplied. The requested modules do not need them; the filings give only quarter-end fair values of the notes, which are not quotes at the as-of date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 19.

- Minor, mitigated: The text rendering flattens tables to one cell per line, so a figure is tied to its row and period only by position. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, pages 81–83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C7.

- Minor, mitigated: The quarter ended December 31, 2025 is stated on its own only as the comparative column of the first-quarter release, and no fourth-quarter release is supplied. Financial foundation should cite that column as the issuer's unaudited figure and take the full year from the annual report.

- Minor, mitigated: Definitions differ between documents. Debt is USD 2,050,000 thousand at principal in the debt note and USD 2,022,758 thousand at carrying value in the balance sheet and releases, and the covenant EBITDA is defined in the credit agreement that is not supplied, while the releases use issuer-adjusted EBITDA. Each leverage figure must name its debt definition, and adjusted EBITDA must not be equated with covenant EBITDA.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C6.
- Minor: No document dated after the third-quarter report's signature on November 4, 2026 is supplied, so any event between that date and the cutoff of November 5, 2026 cannot be checked.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 46.

### Bottom line
Leverage is moderate and lower than at year-end (2.26x total debt to adjusted EBITDA at 2026-09-30), and nothing falls due before 2029, so creditors' near-term exposure is liquidity, not refinancing.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15

That exposure has grown: cash fell by USD 465.64 million in nine months because note redemptions were paid from cash, leaving USD 475.07 million, of which 38.02% sits in the consolidated Saudi joint venture, plus an undrawn USD 350 million revolver.

### Leverage trajectory and drivers

Total debt to adjusted EBITDA fell from 2.73x at year-end 2025 to 2.26x at 2026-09-30, but net debt to adjusted EBITDA moved from 1.70x to 1.73x, so the gross improvement did not reach net leverage. The cause is mechanical: the issuer redeemed the USD 379.15 million 7.50% notes and USD 100.00 million of the 9.125% notes from cash, cutting principal by USD 479.15 million, while cash fell by USD 465.64 million and net debt moved only from USD 1,553.97 million to USD 1,547.69 million. Last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA was USD 912.67 million at year-end and USD 893.57 million at 2026-09-30, so earnings did not drive the change; for creditors the gain is a lower interest bill and no maturity in 2026 to 2028, not a stronger net position.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C10; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 103
### Reported and adjusted EBITDA

The two EBITDA measures point in opposite directions because FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 1,402.13 million contains a USD 413.96 million gain on the Quail Tools sale and a USD 113.65 million bargain purchase gain on the Parker acquisition. Total debt to reported EBITDA therefore looks like 1.78x at year-end and rises to 2.22x by 2026-09-30, while the adjusted ratio falls from 2.73x to 2.26x; by 2026-09-30 the gains have left the twelve-month window and the two ratios sit close together. Adjusted EBITDA is the better trend measure but not a cash one: it excludes Other, net, a cost of USD 65.80 million in FY2025 that included debt buyback losses, severance and impairments, and the issuer itself says the measure excludes certain cash expenses it is obliged to make.

Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C18; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5
### Coverage

Cash interest cover can be stated only for FY2025: 4.36x on adjusted EBITDA and 6.70x on reported EBITDA against USD 209.17 million of cash paid for interest, net of capitalized interest. The interim reports print no cash interest, so for the three 2026 dates the nearest evidence is interest expense, which fell from USD 215.37 million in FY2025 to USD 179.15 million on a twelve-month basis at 2026-09-30 as notes were retired, lifting adjusted EBITDA to interest expense from 4.24x to 4.99x. The issuer reports a credit agreement interest coverage ratio that rose from 4.16x at year-end to 5.20x at 2026-09-30 against a 2.75x minimum, but headroom is not worked here because the covenant's EBITDA definition is not supplied. The four notes outstanding at 2026-09-30 carry coupons of USD 156.75 million a year, covered 5.70x by twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, so cash interest on the current notes should run well below the 2025 level, before revolver fees and other items (analyst judgement).
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C20; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 40
### Cash-flow quality

Operating cash flow for the nine months of 2026 was USD 487.47 million against USD 447.4 million a year earlier, equal to 72.54% of adjusted EBITDA, but capital spending of USD 460.80 million left the issuer's free cash flow at USD 38.65 million, against negative USD 55.85 million in the prior-year period. Receivables are the drag: net receivables rose from USD 391.71 million at year-end to USD 511.66 million, USD 90.5 million of the cash flow change in receivables relates to related parties, 41% of receivables sit in Saudi Arabia, and working capital items used USD 48.3 million in the nine months. The third-quarter release guides full-year adjusted free cash flow of USD 100 million to USD 110 million, including about USD 20 million of cash consumed at SANAD, and USD 60 million to USD 70 million for the fourth quarter, so a large rebuild of cash is not guided.
### Liquidity adequacy

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 475.07 million of cash plus the undrawn USD 350 million revolver, USD 825.07 million in all, down from USD 1,290.71 million at year-end. The joint venture SANAD holds USD 180.64 million, or 38.02%, of consolidated cash, so cash outside it is USD 294.44 million and liquidity on that basis is USD 644.44 million. The revolver can be drawn only while the covenants are met, and the issuer reports compliance. Claims on liquidity include USD 296.4 million of purchase commitments outstanding, fourth-quarter capital spending guided at USD 250 million to USD 260 million, and the receivables purchase agreement, whose term ends no later than 2027-04-01 and under which USD 168.0 million of receivables had been sold and not collected; a lapse without replacement would mean those receivables are funded on the balance sheet, a call of up to that amount on cash or the revolver.

### Debt structure and claims outside debt

All USD 2,050.00 million of principal is fixed-rate notes: USD 250.00 million of 1.75% exchangeable notes due June 2029, USD 550.00 million of 9.125% notes due January 2030, USD 550.00 million of 8.875% notes due August 2031 and USD 700.00 million of 7.625% notes due November 2032. The undrawn revolver, secured by a first lien on land rigs and related equipment, spare parts and inventory in the contiguous United States, matures on 2029-06-17 or 90 days before the exchangeable notes mature if 50% or more of them remain outstanding, so the first dated demand on the structure is in 2029. The exchangeable notes had a fair value of USD 230.31 million, 92.13% of principal, at 2026-09-30. Claims outside the debt figure are the redeemable noncontrolling interest of USD 502.72 million (mezzanine equity, Saudi Aramco's share of the redeemable ownership interests in SANAD, with USD 20.27 million of distributions accrued in nine months), operating lease liabilities of USD 40.21 million at year-end, purchase commitments of USD 296.4 million, letters of credit of USD 133.447 million under bilateral facilities and USD 68.2 million under the credit agreement, financial standby letters of credit and surety instruments of USD 33.795 million at most, which may overlap the letters of credit, receivables sold of USD 168.0 million, and contract liabilities of USD 100.02 million, up from USD 70.57 million at year-end, a non-debt float that helps fund working capital. No pension or retiree medical obligation is separately stated in the balance sheet lines supplied; only pension amortisation appears in other comprehensive income.

Every figure is consolidated for Nabors Industries Ltd. and includes the SANAD joint venture with Saudi Aramco, whose condensed balance sheet shows total assets of USD 1,570.83 million, total liabilities of USD 244.92 million and no debt line; the notes are issued by Nabors Industries, Inc. and guaranteed by Nabors and certain subsidiaries that the documents do not list. ### Strongest contrary evidence

The strongest case against reading leverage as improving is that net debt has not fallen: USD 1,547.69 million against USD 1,553.97 million at year-end, with adjusted EBITDA flat and cash USD 465.64 million lower. SANAD newbuild spending of USD 295 million to USD 305 million is guided for 2026, five SANAD rigs have been suspended, and 41% of receivables are in Saudi Arabia. A fourth quarter below the guided adjusted free cash flow of USD 60 million to USD 70 million, or further rig suspensions that cut adjusted EBITDA, would leave cash falling while net leverage rises; continued adjusted free cash flow near the third-quarter level of USD 74.52 million would support the improving reading.

- Medium: Figures are consolidated and include SANAD, whose cash was USD 180.635 million of USD 475.072 million at 2026-09-30; no obligor-group or restricted-group financials are supplied, so a borrower-level view of cash and EBITDA is not established. Group-level financials would close it.

- Medium: The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA and no FY2025 adjusted EBITDA: reported EBITDA is calculated from components and FY2025 adjusted EBITDA is calculated by the issuer's definition, equal to the stated nine months 2025 plus fourth quarter 2025. The 2025 gains of USD 527.615 million make the reported ratios at the first three dates unsuitable for trend; an issuer statement of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA would confirm it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 82; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_tm2612942d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, pages 6–11; calculation C4.

- Low: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split in any supplied document and cash taxes paid are printed for FY2025 only (USD 73.738 million), so cash flow after maintenance spending and cash tax cover are not established for the 2026 dates. Interim supplemental cash flow disclosures would close it.

- Low: Several statement lines print a dash or are not printed in some columns: the Quail Tools and bargain purchase gains in the 2026 income statements, the current portion of debt, contract liabilities at 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, and a number of cash flow lines (impairments, cash acquired in the Parker business combination, revolver borrowings and repayments, the Parker dividend, SPAC redemptions, the Quail Tools proceeds and the Vast investment). Each is shown as not supplied and none is read as zero; the issuer's own totals and reconciliations show them to be nil.

- Low: The debt note prints no per-instrument carrying value (the fair value note prints principal under that heading) and no revolver reference rate, spread or floor; carrying value is stated in aggregate only, net of deferred financing costs, and the exact maturity days of three of the notes are not printed. The indentures and the credit agreement would close it.

- Low: Fourth quarter 2025 stands alone only as the comparative column of the first-quarter release and is unaudited; it is used in the chart and dashboard, not in any ratio. The fourth-quarter release is not supplied.

- Low: Noncurrent operating lease liabilities are printed for 2025-12-31 only (USD 30.473 million); the interim reports print the current portion alone, so the lease claim at 2026-09-30 is not established. The interim lease note would close it.
- Low: The first and second quarterly reports date the credit agreement joinder April 4, 2026 in the liquidity discussion and April 7, 2026 elsewhere; April 7, 2026 is used and no amount is affected.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Business risk is concentrated in one partner and customer, Saudi Aramco, and governance risk is medium: no holder controls Nabors and 2026 cash went to debt reduction, but related-party dealings, a combined chairman and chief executive, and a joint venture backstop limit creditor protection.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation A6; calculation A11

Saudi Aramco supplied about 30% of 2025 operating revenues and holds USD 502.72 million of redeemable interests in SANAD, the consolidated joint venture that holds 38.02% of group cash (USD 180.64 million), so creditors cannot assume that consolidated cash and earnings are fully available to them.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A5
Ownership, board and pay detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the medium level rests on the filings, not on governance documents.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 132; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- Earnings are anchored in International Drilling and in Saudi Arabia, not spread evenly across four segments. International Drilling produced 50.17% of FY2025 operating revenues and 53.05% in the first nine months of 2026, and Saudi Arabia alone produced about USD 1.0 billion of 2025 revenue, so a Saudi activity cut would move cash flow faster than a change in the U.S. rig count.
Basis: calculation A1; calculation A2; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 123

- Saudi Aramco is customer, joint venture partner and claimant at once, which concentrates counterparty risk on one name. It accounted for approximately 30% of 2025 operating revenues, 31% in 2024 and 26% in 2023, and holds USD 502.72 million of redeemable interests in SANAD outside equity; Nabors must also backstop its share of the first 25 SANAD rig purchases if the venture lacks cash or financing, and a change of control could trigger a call option to purchase its SANAD interest. A dispute or contract cut with this one counterparty would reach revenue, cash and the joint venture at the same time.

- Contract terms give limited protection to revenue. Most contracts are daywork contracts at a dayrate, term contracts last from six months to five years, single-well contracts can be ended on short notice, and early termination payments may not fully compensate; no backlog or rig-level contract schedule is supplied, so durability is judged from rig counts and margins only.

- Capital allocation has favoured creditors in 2026, not clearly in 2025. In the first nine months of 2026 principal fell by USD 479.15 million, paid from cash on hand, while in 2025 the USD 902.68 million of debt repaid was largely refinanced with USD 700.0 million of new notes and revolver borrowings, leaving principal only USD 10.46 million lower. The issuer paid no common dividend in the cash flow statements for 2023 to 2025, bought Parker with shares and USD 0.6 million of cash, and sold Quail Tools for net consideration of USD 600.0 million. The restraint is a choice, not a limit: the September 2025 amendment lets the issuer repurchase up to USD 100.0 million of equity each fiscal year, so capacity to distribute exists although none has been used.

- Governance leaves authority concentrated and related parties active, and the proxy statement that would show board independence is not supplied. One person is chairman, president and chief executive and the chief operating decision maker; a company he owns and manages is a member of Hexegen LLC, which received energy transition assets from Nabors and would share profits with Nabors above a threshold, up to a 90:10 split; a director's group billed USD 14.8 million for services in 2025; and managers and directors co-sponsor Nabors' SPAC. None of these items is quantified as leakage, but together they weaken the independent check on capital allocation.

- Cash is not freely upstreamed to note holders. Nabors is a holding company that relies on its subsidiaries and investments, its debt instruments do not forbid contractual limits on upstream payments, and 38.02% of consolidated cash (USD 180.64 million) sits in SANAD, whose liabilities carry no recourse to other Nabors assets, so group cash overstates what is available to creditors of the borrower.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation A5

- The joint venture is also a call on cash. SANAD newbuild capital spending is guided at USD 295 million to USD 305 million for 2026 with about USD 20 million of cash consumed at SANAD, one further newbuild is due in 2026 and two in the first quarter of 2027, and five SANAD rigs have been suspended, so some of that spending adds capacity while other rigs are idle (analyst interpretation).
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a lower governance risk is the debt reduction and the absence of a sponsor or common dividend: cash that could have gone to shareholders cut principal by USD 479.15 million in the first nine months of 2026, the auditor's opinion on the annual statements and on internal control is unqualified, and the issuer reports compliance with its credit agreement covenants. The strongest evidence for a higher risk is the concentration in Saudi Aramco and the open joint venture backstop. A proxy statement showing an independent board majority and a separate chair, or indentures showing guarantee and restricted payment terms no wider than the credit agreement's, would move the level toward low; a renegotiation or cut of Saudi Aramco work, use of the USD 100.0 million annual repurchase capacity, or a call on the backstop would move it toward high.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee structure, holdings above 5% and executive pay are not established; this holds the governance level at medium and prevents any statement about director independence.

- The joint venture agreement, the contracts with Saudi Aramco, the indentures and the credit agreement are not supplied, so the call option, the backstop, restricted payment capacity and guarantor coverage are known only from filing summaries; conclusions about the partner's leverage over Nabors and about distribution capacity are bounded accordingly.

- No customer backlog, contract expiry schedule or rig-level dayrate is supplied, so the view of revenue durability rests on segment results and rig counts, and concentration beyond Saudi Aramco cannot be tested.

Quail Tools, a Parker business, was sold on 2025-08-20 to Superior Energy Services for USD 375.0 million of cash and a USD 250.0 million seller note that was prepaid in full on 2025-10-09; the gain was USD 413.96 million and the sale raised the 2025 tax provision by USD 96.9 million, while the third-quarter 2025 comparison shows USD 20.305 million of adjusted EBITDA that has left the business.

New debt in the period was one issue: USD 700.0 million of 7.625% senior priority guaranteed notes due November 2032, issued on 2025-11-10, whose proceeds redeemed all of the 7.375% notes due May 2027 (USD 546.1 million outstanding, redeemed for about USD 557.1 million); the issuer also redeemed USD 164.4 million of Nabors Delaware notes in 2025, called the 7.50% notes due January 2028 on 2025-12-24 (redeemed on 2026-01-15 for about USD 393.4 million including accrued interest) and redeemed USD 100.0 million of the 9.125% notes due January 2030 for about USD 104.9 million in the third quarter of 2026.

The credit agreement was amended twice: on 2025-09-04 to allow equity repurchases of up to USD 100.0 million a fiscal year, with dividends reducing that capacity dollar for dollar, and on 2026-04-07 to raise the letter of credit tranche by USD 25.0 million to USD 150.0 million; the USD 350.0 million revolver is undrawn and matures on 2029-06-17 or earlier if the exchangeable notes stay outstanding.

Other transactions are the equity-funded purchase of Quaise Energy preferred stock on 2026-08-26 for 0.4 million Nabors shares worth USD 35.0 million, and the settlement on 2025-10-14 of the dispute between the Nabors SPAC and e2 for a secured note of USD 29.23 million; no further acquisition, divestiture or sponsor transaction is stated, and nothing after 2026-11-04 is supplied.

- High: The proxy statement for the 2026 annual general meeting is not supplied, so board independence, committee structure, holders above 5% and executive pay are not established and the governance level stays at medium. The proxy statement would close it.

- High: The joint venture agreement and the contracts with Saudi Aramco are not supplied, so the call option, the backstop and the terms of the redeemable interests are known only from filing summaries and the partner's leverage over Nabors cannot be sized. The executed agreement would close it.

- High: The indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so restricted payment capacity, guarantor coverage and the ranking and security of the notes are not established beyond the filing summaries. The executed documents would close it.

- Medium: Amounts and approval terms for the Hexegen profit sharing and the director-affiliated services are not stated beyond the USD 14.8 million of services in 2025, so related-party leakage cannot be sized. The proxy statement's related-person section would close it.

- Medium: No customer backlog, contract expiry schedule or rig-level dayrate is supplied, so revenue durability and concentration beyond Saudi Aramco cannot be tested. Customer contract schedules would close it.

- Medium: The dates and contract effect of the five SANAD rig suspensions are not stated, so the near-term earnings effect of the newbuild program cannot be dated. The next release or investor presentation would close it.

- Low: The use of the Quail Tools proceeds and the funding source of each redemption are not itemised, so the link between asset-sale cash and debt reduction is inferred from the cash flow statement. The cash flow notes would close it.

- Low: The consideration for the Quail Tools sale is stated as net consideration of USD 600.0 million, while cash of USD 375.0 million and a seller note of USD 250.0 million add to USD 625.0 million; the difference is not explained and the cash flow statement shows USD 622.856 million of proceeds. The sale agreement would close it.

- Low: Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split, so free cash flow durability after the SANAD newbuild program is not established. Management discussion or investor materials would close it.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Nabors presents an adequate but only partly assessable credit profile: scale, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before 2029 support creditors, while thin free cash flow, one-partner concentration and unestablished note priority constrain it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F7

At 2026-09-30 total debt was 2.26x and net debt 1.73x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 893.57 million, liquidity was USD 825.07 million including cash held in the SANAD joint venture, and issuer-defined free cash flow over the last four quarters was only USD 170.44 million. The primary downside path is a cut in Saudi Arabian activity, which would reach revenue, joint venture cash and covenants together.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F4; calculation F6
A firmer opinion needs the indentures, the credit agreement, the proxy statement and the joint venture agreement, none of which is supplied.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- Leverage is moderate and falling on the adjusted measure: total debt to adjusted EBITDA was 2.73x at year-end 2025 and 2.26x at 2026-09-30, and interest expense over the last twelve months fell to USD 179.15 million from USD 215.37 million in FY2025, so adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense 4.99x. The fall came from paying down notes with cash, not from earnings, so net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 1.73x against 1.70x at year-end; on reported EBITDA, which Financial foundation calculates, the ratios at 2026-09-30 are 2.22x total and 1.70x net, so the choice of definition moves total leverage by only 0.04x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F5

- Refinancing risk is deferred, not removed: no principal falls due before 2029, then USD 250.00 million in 2029 and USD 550.00 million in 2030, together 0.90 times last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, with a further USD 550.00 million in 2031 and USD 700.00 million in 2032. The undrawn USD 350 million revolver matures on 2029-06-17, or earlier if half or more of the exchangeable notes remain outstanding shortly before their own maturity, so the first real test is a 2029 refinancing by an issuer whose senior unsecured debt is rated non-investment grade and whose note collateral, guarantor list and ranking between note classes are not set out.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 16

- Free cash flow is the weakest link between earnings and debt service. Operating cash flow was 72.54% of adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026, but capital spending of USD 460.80 million, 18.65% of revenue and driven by SANAD newbuilds, left free cash flow at USD 38.65 million after USD 11.98 million of asset sale proceeds; after net capital spending of USD 562.87 million over four quarters, adjusted EBITDA less capital spending covers interest expense 1.85x. Management guides full-year adjusted free cash flow of USD 100 million to USD 110 million, so deleveraging beyond the 2026 paydown depends on capital spending falling after the newbuild program.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F6; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Liquidity is adequate but overstated by consolidation: cash plus the undrawn revolver was USD 825.07 million at 2026-09-30, USD 644.44 million excluding the 38.02% of cash held in SANAD, and the receivables purchase agreement that funds USD 168.0 million of sold receivables ends no later than 2027-04-01. The covenant interest coverage ratio reported at 5.20x against a 2.75x minimum is a comfort, but the covenant's EBITDA is not defined in the documents supplied.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 40

- The business is large and technology-led but concentrated: International Drilling is 53.05% of nine-month 2026 revenue, Saudi Aramco was about 30% of 2025 revenue and is also the joint venture partner, and customers can end single-well contracts at short notice. Adjusted EBITDA margin has held between 26.14% and 28.15% across the last four quarters and adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 245.54 million in the third quarter of 2026, so earnings are improving, but their durability past the 2026 guidance of about USD 930.00 million is not testable without backlog data.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F2; calculation F8; calculation F9; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Governance and structure add monitoring risk rather than a distinct default driver: authority is concentrated in a combined chairman and chief executive, related-party dealings are unquantified, and Nabors is a holding company whose upstream cash is not contractually assured, but no sponsor extracts cash, no common dividend is paid and gross debt has been reduced. The sponsor and governance risk level is medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger credit is the pace of operating improvement and the deferral of maturities: quarterly adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 221.56 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 to USD 245.54 million in the third quarter of 2026, management guides about USD 930.00 million for 2026 and an annualised run rate near USD 1 billion going into 2027, no principal falls due before 2029, and the interest coverage ratio reported to lenders rose from 4.16x to 5.20x. The strongest evidence for a weaker credit is that net leverage has not fallen, free cash flow is small after growth capital spending, and about half of revenue is international with one counterparty at its centre. A fourth quarter at or above the guided adjusted free cash flow of USD 60 million to USD 70 million, a fall in capital spending after the newbuild program, and a renewed receivables purchase agreement would support the stronger reading; further SANAD rig suspensions, a Saudi payment delay, or a refinancing of the 2029 notes that needs a higher coupon would support the weaker one.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation F1; calculation F6; calculation F9
### Limitations

- Free cash flow is judged from issuer-defined figures for four quarters and management guidance for 2026; the split between maintenance and growth capital spending is not supplied, so the view that capital spending can fall after the newbuild program is not tested and the free cash flow assessment stays weak rather than average.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Note collateral, the guarantor list, the ranking between note classes and the covenant definitions are not set out beyond filing summaries, so the statements on refinancing capacity and covenant comfort cannot be turned into a recovery or headroom view; both are left to the modules that read executed documents.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15

- No peer set, agency rating or dated market price is supplied, so the profile is described against the issuer's own history and not against other leveraged drillers, and the adequate assessment is not a rating-style ranking.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

Scale and service breadth give Nabors earnings capacity: it owns one of the world's largest land rig fleets and also operates offshore platform rigs, four segments contributed to last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA of USD 893.57 million, and quarterly adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 204.81 million in the first quarter of 2026 to USD 245.54 million in the third, so debt service rests on a broad operating base, not a single rig class.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F2; calculation F8

No principal falls due before 2029 and the USD 350 million revolver is undrawn, so the group can absorb a weak quarter without a refinancing event; this lowers near-term default probability even though it does not remove the 2029 and 2030 refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F3; calculation F7

Gross debt and interest expense have been cut: principal fell from USD 2,529.15 million at year-end 2025 to USD 2,050.00 million at 2026-09-30, and last-twelve-months interest expense fell to USD 179.15 million, which raises interest coverage and widens the margin for error under the 2.75x covenant minimum.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F3; calculation F5

Operating momentum is positive: average rigs working rose from the second quarter to the third quarter of 2026 and International Drilling reached a record daily adjusted gross margin of USD 19,060, which supports guided fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA growth.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation F9

Capital allocation has not extracted cash: there is no sponsor, no common dividend in the 2023 to 2026 cash flow statements, Parker was bought with shares, and gross debt has fallen since Quail Tools was sold, which means no sponsor or shareholder claim competes with note holders for cash.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 13
Weaknesses.

One partner concentrates risk: Saudi Aramco was approximately 30% of 2025 revenue, is the SANAD partner and holds USD 502.72 million of redeemable interests, so a change in its activity or terms would move revenue, joint venture cash and the backstop at once, and the weight of International Drilling in revenue is 53.05%.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F11

Free cash flow is thin and volatile: issuer-defined free cash flow was negative in the first quarter of 2026 and USD 74.52 million in the third, USD 170.44 million over four quarters, against USD 2,022.76 million of debt, so deleveraging depends on capital spending falling after the SANAD newbuild program.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F6; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 12

Liquidity is overstated by consolidation and funding that can lapse: 38.02% of cash sits in SANAD, USD 168.0 million of receivables are sold under an agreement that ends no later than 2027-04-01, and letters of credit and purchase commitments of USD 296.4 million call on the same resources.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F4; calculation F11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 42

Structural clarity is missing: the filings label the 2030 and 2032 notes senior priority guaranteed, the 2031 notes senior guaranteed and the 2029 notes senior exchangeable, but the collateral, the full list of guarantors and the ranking between those classes are not set out; Nabors is a holding company reliant on subsidiary cash, its senior unsecured debt is rated non-investment grade, and USD 502.72 million of redeemable interests sit outside debt and equity, so recovery and priority cannot be judged from the documents supplied.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 15

Governance concentrates authority and tolerates related-party dealings that are not sized, and the proxy statement that would show board independence is not supplied, so monitoring rather than comfort is the right posture.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

### Company description

Nabors is a Bermuda holding company that owns one of the largest land drilling fleets and offshore platform rigs, sells drilling technology and tubular running services, and makes rig equipment; its borrower is Nabors Industries, Inc. Revenue of USD 3,268.07 million over the last twelve months comes from four segments, International Drilling is the largest at 53.05% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and 58.88% of FY2025 revenue arose outside the United States. Daywork contracts at a dayrate dominate, so cash flow follows rig count and daily margin, not volume commitments; this gives visibility only for the length of a term contract, which runs from six months to five years, and no backlog is supplied.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation F2; calculation F10

History matters for the credit: Parker was acquired for shares on 2025-03-11 and Quail Tools was sold on 2025-08-20, so the earnings base after the sale is smaller than FY2025 and debt was reduced afterwards; the Quail Tools gain of USD 413.96 million and the Parker gain of USD 113.65 million inflate reported FY2025 EBITDA but not adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F12
### Ownership and group structure

Nabors is a public company with no controlling holder identified: officers, directors and holders of 5% or more together held about 4.49% of shares at 2025-06-30, former Parker holders vote with the Board under lock-up agreements, and no sponsor fee, recapitalisation or common dividend is stated. The borrower and note issuer is a wholly owned subsidiary, the notes are guaranteed by Nabors and subsidiaries that are not listed, and the SANAD joint venture is half owned by Saudi Aramco and fully consolidated, so the borrower's creditors reach SANAD cash only through what the venture distributes after meeting its own liabilities, while its partner holds USD 502.72 million of redeemable interests.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation F14
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, partly concentrated and pricing-sensitive: operators award most work by bid, competition is price-led with excess rig supply historically, and US operators have kept activity flat while gaining drilling efficiency, so rig counts need not rise with the oil price. Against that, leading-edge Lower 48 pricing is rising, average rigs working rose from the second quarter to the third quarter of 2026, and International Drilling's daily adjusted gross margin rose to USD 19,060, so margin per rig day, not rig count, is the near-term driver. Saudi Aramco's per-rig contracts at about 30% of FY2025 revenue make Saudi activity the single largest revenue sensitivity.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 7; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Cost structure and margin resilience

The cost base is heavy in assets and variable in direct costs: direct costs were 62.24% of nine-month 2026 revenue, depreciation and amortization 19.29% and general and administrative 8.90%, so a revenue decline falls through to EBITDA quickly while depreciation does not flex. Adjusted EBITDA margin moved from 27.78% to 26.14%, 27.20% and 28.15% over the last four quarters, which shows margins can be defended when rig activity and margin per day rise together; resilience to a fall in activity is not tested because no downturn quarter is in the window.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F8; calculation F13
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital intensity is high and rising with the SANAD program: capital expenditures were USD 460.80 million, 18.65% of nine-month 2026 revenue, against operating cash flow of USD 487.47 million, and management guides full-year capital spending of USD 710 million to USD 720 million including USD 295 million to USD 305 million for SANAD newbuilds. Working capital absorbed USD 48.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 while net receivables rose, cash interest paid was USD 209.17 million in FY2025, and maintenance spending is not separated, so conversion of EBITDA to cash available for debt service is about 5.75% of adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026 and rises only if growth capital spending is cut.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F6; calculation F14; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is intense and sets pricing: the annual report names Helmerich & Payne, Patterson-UTI, Precision and Ensign as rivals and says contracts are mostly bid, so pricing power is limited to periods of tight supply. New entry is limited by the capital needed for modern rigs, but rigs move between regions, so excess capacity can be imported; substitution takes the form of efficiency and automation, which lower the number of rigs needed per unit of output. Buyers are large and informed, and Saudi Aramco is both buyer and joint venture owner, which gives it more leverage than a normal customer; supplier power is low for rig equipment because Nabors makes its own through Canrig.
### PEST analysis

Political and economic factors are a primary credit driver: the Middle East conflict has disrupted regional exports, raised crude prices and led operators to place rigs on standby and issue suspension notices, five SANAD rigs have been suspended, Argentina's economy is classified as highly inflationary under U.S. accounting rules, and a rig deployment in Venezuela is planned for early 2027. Interest rates and oil prices set customers' spending; social and technology factors are secondary to credit, apart from automation that lowers rigs needed.
### SWOT

Strengths for creditors are scale, the undrawn revolver, no maturity before 2029 and falling gross debt; weaknesses are thin free cash flow, one-partner concentration, unestablished note priority and holding company structure. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are guided run-rate adjusted EBITDA near USD 1 billion going into 2027, lower capital spending after the SANAD program and margin gains from technology; threats are further suspensions in Saudi Arabia, an oil price fall, a lapse of the receivables programme and a costly 2029 refinancing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation F1; calculation F7
### Financial profile and credit quality

Against the nine dimensions the profile reads: scale and market position strong; competitive advantage average, because technology claims are management statements and no market share is supplied; business diversification average, held back by the weight of International Drilling and Saudi Aramco; cost and capex flexibility average, because growth spending at SANAD is discretionary beyond the backstop but maintenance spending is not separated; margin stability average, with margins between 26.14% and 28.15% over four quarters; free cash flow stability weak, as quarterly issuer-defined free cash flow ran from negative USD 48.22 million to USD 131.80 million; ability to refinance average, since USD 700.00 million of notes were issued in November 2025 but the senior unsecured rating is non-investment grade and the ranking between note classes is not set out; liquidity position average, with USD 825.07 million of cash plus revolver but 38.02% of cash in SANAD; financial policy and governance average, supported by debt reduction and no dividend but limited by concentrated authority and a missing proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F4; calculation F6; calculation F8
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next one to two years management guides 2026 adjusted EBITDA of about USD 930.00 million, which implies USD 257.98 million in the fourth quarter against USD 245.54 million in the third, adjusted free cash flow of USD 100 million to USD 110 million, and further Lower 48 gains; headwinds are the SANAD suspensions, lower international rig counts of 92 to 93 in the fourth quarter, and working capital tied up in Saudi receivables. Over three to five years the notes maturing from 2029 to 2032 total USD 2,050.00 million, and the 2029 and 2030 maturities alone are 0.90 times last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, so refinancing capacity depends on holding adjusted EBITDA near the 2026 run rate and on leverage staying near 2.26x.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F1; calculation F7; calculation F9; calculation F14
### Downside scenario

The issuer-specific downside begins with a cut in Saudi Arabian activity: the Middle East conflict has already led operators to issue suspension notices and five SANAD rigs are suspended, so a wider cut would first lower rig days and daily margin in International Drilling, 53.05% of revenue. Because direct costs are 62.24% of revenue and depreciation does not flex, EBITDA would fall faster than revenue; free cash flow, already thin at USD 38.65 million over nine months, would turn negative unless capital spending falls, and receivables from Saudi Arabia, 41% of the balance, would rise as payment slows. Liquidity of USD 825.07 million would fall as cash funds the gap, and the receivables programme ending by 2027-04-01 could add up to USD 168.0 million of funding need; management can cut growth capital spending at SANAD, but the backstop of the first 25 rigs limits that lever. Leverage would rise toward the covenant tests, whose definitions are not supplied, but no maturity falls due before 2029, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within twelve months and the first observable triggers are further suspensions, Saudi collections and fourth-quarter free cash flow.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nbr-20260930x10q.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_tm2628332d1_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F4; calculation F6; calculation F11
### Overall credit view

Overall, Nabors presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, technology breadth, an undrawn revolver and no maturity before 2029, but credit quality is constrained by thin free cash flow, concentration in Saudi Aramco and the SANAD joint venture, and note priority that is not established. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because issuer-defined free cash flow was USD 170.44 million over four quarters. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding adjusted EBITDA near USD 930.00 million, cutting growth capital spending after the newbuild program, and renewing the receivables programme. The primary downside path is a cut in Saudi activity reaching revenue, joint venture cash and covenants together. Further analysis would require the indentures, the credit agreement, the joint venture agreement and the proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation F6; calculation F9

## Gaps

- High: The indentures and the credit agreement are not supplied, so the collateral, the full list of guarantors and the ranking between note classes, the covenant definitions and the restricted payment terms are not established; refinancing capacity and covenant comfort are therefore stated without a priority or headroom view. The executed documents would close it.
- High: Cash paid for interest is printed only for FY2025, so cash interest cover for 2026 is not established and the interest expense ratios are proxies. Interim cash interest paid would close it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 121.

- Medium: No backlog amount, contract expiry schedule or rig-level dayrate is supplied (the second-quarter release says only that Lower 48 backlog duration was extended), so revenue durability beyond the 2026 guidance is not testable. Customer contract schedules would close it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_tm2621313d2_ex99-1.htm.jsonl, page 2.

- Medium: The joint venture agreement and the Saudi Aramco contracts are not supplied, so the call option, the backstop and the partner's claims are known only from summaries and the downside effect on creditors cannot be sized. The executed agreement would close it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nbr-20251231x10k.htm.jsonl, page 114.

- Medium: The split between maintenance and growth capital spending is not supplied, so the capital spending that can be cut in a downturn is not established. Management discussion or investor materials would close it.

- Medium: No peer set, agency rating, market price or portfolio is supplied, so the profile cannot be placed against other leveraged drillers or priced. Peer filings, agency reports and dated quotes would close it.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0).

- Low: The dates of the five SANAD rig suspensions and the date of the Middle East conflict developments that drove them are not stated, so the timing of the earnings effect is not established. The next quarterly release would close it.

- Low: Management guidance covers only the fourth quarter of 2026 and the full year, so the outlook beyond 2026 uses a run-rate statement near USD 1 billion that is management's view and not a forecast of this analysis.
